stories.tag: US - AI pilot failure / data readiness
stories.title: Gartner: Only 13% of CIOs Report Significant AI Value; Use Case Success Rate Remains One-in-Five
stories.body: At Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo in Orlando on October 19, 2026, Gartner released survey data showing only 13% of CIOs say their enterprise has realized significant or transformational value from AI. Despite AI use cases accelerating over two years, the likelihood of any single use case succeeding remains one-in-five. A separate Gartner finding reinforces the root cause: 85% of AI projects fail due to poor underlying data quality, and projects lacking AI-ready data are at serious risk of abandonment.
stories.why: This is the single most powerful objection-handling stat a Graas seller can use: AI investment is near-universal yet value realization is at 13% — and the cause is data quality and context, not model capability. It directly validates why a governed semantic/context layer must precede any agent deployment, which is exactly what Graas enables.

stories.tag: US - McKinsey analyst report / CPG agentic AI
stories.title: McKinsey (Oct 9, 2026): For CPG Companies, Agentic AI's Real Payoff Is Growth — Not Cost-Cutting
stories.body: McKinsey's October 9, 2026 article, based on a survey of 41 senior commercial leaders across large CPG companies in the US and Europe, argues that CPG businesses are leaving growth on the table by deploying agentic AI primarily to cut costs and speed up existing work rather than as a growth accelerator. The firm contends the real opportunity lies in the increasingly complex CPG-retailer relationship, and that agentic AI must be deployed across the full commercial system — innovation, marketing, revenue growth management, and execution — to recapture lost sales. McKinsey separately found that in its 2026 State of AI survey, 80% of respondents report AI improved individual productivity, yet only 37% report positive EBIT impact.
stories.why: This McKinsey article arms a Graas seller with a named consultancy's argument that productivity pilots are not enough — agents must be wired into commercial workflows end-to-end to generate revenue lift, the exact framing Graas uses. The 37% EBIT figure confirms the pilot-to-production gap is still wide and traceable to workflow and data-foundation gaps.

stories.tag: Global - BCG named deployment / CPG supply chain agents
stories.title: BCG: Global CPG Leader Deploys Agentic Replenishment System, Cuts Admin Costs 40–60% and Lifts Fill Rates
stories.body: BCG's June 2026 report 'The AI-First Supply Chain' documents a global consumer goods company that replaced reactive, backward-looking analytics with a multi-agent replenishment system. Supply chain managers empowered by AI agents saw fill rates and in-stock levels rise by 2–4 percentage points, while administration costs fell 40%–60%. The modular architecture routes recommendations through subagents for data mapping, rationale tracking, and validation, with human analysts retained in the loop for critical decisions.
stories.why: This is a named, outcome-quantified BCG case study a Graas seller can put in front of a CPG or distributor prospect to show agents working in an actual replenishment workflow — not a pilot. The modular agent architecture described maps directly to Graas's own layered approach, and the in-stock and fill-rate outcomes are KPIs every supply chain buyer tracks.

stories.tag: US - BCG analyst report / retailer agentic commerce strategy
stories.title: BCG (Oct 21, 2026): 68% of Retailers Expect Agentic Commerce to Be Transformational Within Two Years
stories.body: BCG's October 21, 2026 article, based on a survey of 150 retailers and brands, finds 68% expect AI shopping agents to have a significant or transformational effect on commerce within two years. Eight in ten retailers have already taken a formal position on external agents: 42% make their product data discoverable by any agent, 32% allow access only to chosen agents, and 6% are blocking agents entirely. BCG argues retailers must now win both the direct shopper visit and the agent's recommendation — placing different demands on data quality, pricing consistency, and fulfillment reliability.
stories.why: This BCG report reframes 'agent readiness' as a commercial survival question for any retailer or brand: if an agent cannot read your product, pricing, and inventory data cleanly, it routes demand to a competitor. Graas sellers can use this to open a conversation about whether a prospect's data layer is machine-readable — today, not in two years.

stories.tag: US - enterprise AI architecture / context layer critique
stories.title: Snowflake, Atlan, Databricks: Q1–Q3 2026 Vendor Wave Frames the 'Context Layer' as the Core Enterprise AI Infrastructure Product
stories.body: A growing body of 2026 vendor and analyst output — led by Snowflake's published architecture, Atlan's Enterprise Data Graph, and Databricks/Snowplow's real-time framing — defines the context layer as the architectural tier between raw enterprise data and AI agents that translates data into governed business meaning agents can act on reliably. Snowflake's architecture predicted 'agent context, not the model, will be the core product as the model gets commoditized.' Gartner has published multiple 2026 analyses describing context layers as an architectural interaction plane for agents and as infrastructure for creating reusable context across agents, while a dbt Labs April 2026 benchmark found a semantic layer scored 98–100% accuracy versus 84–90% for text-to-SQL on enterprise questions.
stories.why: This story gives a Graas seller a vendor-neutral, analyst-backed vocabulary to explain why agents fail without a context layer — and why the context layer, not the LLM, is the enterprise buying decision. The dbt accuracy benchmark is a crisp proof point that structured semantic layers outperform raw model inference on real enterprise data.
